questions.question: As you approach a Give Way line, what should you do?
options: Slow down early so you can stop if traffic is coming
Keep your speed until the last metre
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 tells drivers to approach under control ready to give way.

questions.question: When a lane ahead is closed by cones, when should you merge?
options: Early and smoothly when you see a safe gap
At the very last cone by forcing in
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 advises changing lanes smoothly in good time.

questions.question: Does an entering car have priority over a car already on the roundabout?
options: No, traffic already on the roundabout from the right has priority
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 gives priority to circulating traffic from the right.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on a roundabout?
options: Stay on and go clockwise all the way around again
Stop and reverse back to the exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says never reverse or turn back; simply go around clockwise.

questions.question: If another car is circulating alongside you in the next lane, what must you avoid?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 warns against drifting into another lane on roundabouts.

questions.question: Where can you check which lane leads to your exit before reaching a busy roundabout?
options: Advance signs and painted arrows on the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to read signs and road markings early.

questions.question: What do dashed white spiral lines on a large roundabout show?
options: Which lane path to follow to reach your exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses lane markings to guide traffic smoothly around large roundabouts.

questions.question: When taking the third exit to the right at a two-lane roundabout, which lane is usual?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses the right-hand lane for exits to the right unless signed otherwise.

questions.question: What do the white zig-zag lines beside a pedestrian crossing mean?
options: You must not park or overtake there
You may park for five minutes
You must speed up past the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids parking and overtaking within crossing zig-zag lines.

questions.question: When may you enter a yellow criss-cross box junction to go straight ahead?
options: Whenever the traffic lights are green
Only when your exit road is clear
When the car ahead is still moving slowly
At any time if you signal
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 states you must not enter a box junction unless your exit is clear.

questions.question: At speeds up to 30 mph, how much side space should you leave when overtaking a cyclist?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 says to leave at least 1.5 metres when overtaking cyclists up to 30 mph.

questions.question: What minimum gap should you leave behind the car in front on a dry road?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 sets at least a two-second gap in dry conditions.

questions.question: When should you give a signal before turning or changing lanes?
options: In good time before you make the move
Only when another car is behind you
Only at night or in rain
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 tells you to give clear signals in good time.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car in a built-up area with street lights, unless signed otherwise?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets 30 mph as the standard built-up area limit for cars.

questions.question: What signal should you give on approach when turning left at a roundabout?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires signalling left on approach when taking the first exit.

questions.question: When going straight ahead at a roundabout, when should you signal left?
options: Just after you pass the exit before the one you want
After you have left the roundabout
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says to signal left after passing the exit before yours.

questions.question: May you overtake the leading car that has stopped at a zebra crossing?
options: Yes, if you cannot see anyone on the stripes
No, you must not overtake the leading vehicle
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 states you must never overtake the moving or stopped lead vehicle at a crossing.

questions.question: What problem happens if you enter a box junction without a clear exit?
options: You could block cross traffic when the lights change
Your tyres lose grip on the yellow paint
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 keeps box junctions clear so cross traffic is not trapped.

questions.question: When driving faster than 30 mph, what should you do when overtaking a cyclist?
options: Leave even more space than 1.5 metres
Pass closer so it takes less time
Sound your horn just before passing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 advises giving cyclists even more room at speeds over 30 mph.

questions.question: How do you check the two-second rule while driving?
options: Count two seconds after the car ahead passes a fixed landmark
Leave two car lengths at every speed
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 explains counting two seconds from a fixed point the car ahead passes.

questions.question: If your indicator bulb fails before a drive, what should you do?
options: Fix it before driving, or use clear arm signals if safe
Use hazard lights for every turn
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 includes arm signals when indicators are not working.

questions.question: When you see temporary orange or red 50 mph roadworks signs, what is the legal limit?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 applies to temporary mandatory speed limits at roadworks.

questions.question: If the roundabout is completely clear to your right, must you still stop?
options: No, keep moving smoothly if it is safe and clear
Yes, stop for three seconds every time
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 requires giving way, not stopping unnecessarily when the way is clear.

questions.question: When pulling away from the side of the road, when should you signal?
options: Before you pull away, if other road users could benefit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 advises signalling in good time when pulling away.

questions.question: Why should you often drive slower than the speed limit?
options: Roadworks, rain, bends, or parked cars can make the limit unsafe
Because speed limits are just suggestions
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 and 125 state the limit is a maximum, not a target.

questions.question: You are approaching a crossing and see a cyclist ahead inside the zig-zag lines. What should you do?
options: Hold back behind the cyclist until past the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids overtaking any vehicle inside the zig-zag zone.

questions.question: You are turning right at a box junction, and the road you want to turn into is jammed full. May you enter the box?
options: No, because your exit road is blocked
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 only allows waiting in the box if your exit road itself is clear.

questions.question: Who else needs similar wide clearance and slow passing speeds under Rule 163 / 215?
options: Horse riders and pedestrians walking in the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 gives wide, slow clearance to cyclists, horse riders, and walkers.

questions.question: When you stop in a queue behind another car, how much space should you leave?
options: Enough to see their rear tyres on the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 and queueing advice keep space to steer around if needed.

questions.question: Why should you check that your indicator has cancelled after a gentle bend?
options: Self-cancelling switches may not turn off after a small steer
It is required only on motorways
Indicators turn off after two flashes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 reminds you to cancel signals manually if they stay on.

questions.question: What tells you a 20 mph zone has ended?
options: A sign showing the new limit, such as 30
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 requires following the signed limit until a new limit sign appears.

questions.question: If the traffic light is green but the exit past the box is full, what could happen if you enter?
options: You will be stuck in the box when the cross traffic gets a green light
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 prevents drivers getting trapped across live junctions.

questions.question: What phrase helps drivers count two seconds cleanly?
options: Say 'Only a fool breaks the two-second rule'
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 suggests a steady two-second count past a fixed landmark.

questions.question: When must you stop completely behind a solid white line with a red octagonal STOP sign?
options: Every time, even if the road looks clear
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 171 and Rule 172 require a full stop at a STOP sign and line.

questions.question: Why should you look over your shoulder before moving into another lane?
options: Because mirrors do not show every blind spot
To wave thank you to cars behind
To see if your brake lights work
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 warns that mirrors cannot cover every blind spot beside your car.

questions.question: Why should you avoid signalling left too early when going straight ahead?
options: Waiting drivers may think you are taking the first exit and pull out
It is illegal on motorways only
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 avoids early left signals so waiting traffic is not misled.

questions.question: Who benefits most from a clear left exit signal on a roundabout?
options: Drivers waiting at the next entrance to join the roundabout
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses exit signals to show waiting drivers you are leaving.

questions.question: At a painted mini-roundabout, how should you pass the white circle when turning right?
options: Drive clockwise around the painted circle if possible
Cut straight across the wrong side of the circle
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 188 and Rule 185 state all vehicles must pass around the central marking clockwise.

questions.question: What if a pedestrian is waiting to cross the side road you are turning into?
options: Give way and let them cross safely
Wave them back and turn fast
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 170 and Rule 172 require giving way to pedestrians crossing side roads.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes without checking your blind spot?
options: You could hit a cyclist, rider, or car beside you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 highlights that motorcycles and cars can hide in blind spots.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, three cars arrive at once and nobody has clear priority. What should you do?
options: Make eye contact, proceed slowly, and give way if unsure
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and courtesy advice help resolve deadlocks safely.

questions.question: Can large lorries sometimes touch the edge of a painted mini-roundabout circle?
options: Yes, long vehicles may need to, but cars must drive around it clockwise
Only cars may drive over it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 note cars must pass around the circle clockwise.

questions.question: On a dual-lane exit roundabout where both lanes lead straight ahead, how should you pick your approach lane?
options: Use the left lane unless you are overtaking or signs direct otherwise
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 keeps traffic left unless overtaking or directed by markings.

questions.question: A lorry on the roundabout is taking the next exit, blocking your view of the lane behind it. What should you do?
options: Wait until the lorry clears so you can see any hidden vehicles behind it
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 warns not to enter when a large vehicle hides traffic to your right.

questions.question: You are visiting from a right-hand-driving country. What habit must you watch at UK roundabouts?
options: Do not turn anti-clockwise onto the roundabout; keep left and go clockwise
Sound your horn at every exit
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 reminds newcomers that UK roundabouts always go clockwise.

questions.question: What if a cyclist ahead is in the left lane and intends to turn right at the roundabout?
options: Give them room and do not overtake closely on the approach
Squeeze past them on the left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 warns that cyclists may stay in the left lane even when turning right.

questions.question: If a main road has two lanes in one direction and you turn left onto it, which lane should you join?
options: The left-hand lane unless road signs say otherwise
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 172 and lane rules keep turning traffic in the left lane when clear.

questions.question: You see a motorcycle filtering between lanes as you plan to move right. What should you do?
options: Steer right anyway because you are bigger
Hold your lane and wait until the rider has passed safely
Open your door to warn them
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 requires watching for motorcyclists before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why must you watch the outer lane carefully when joining a two-lane roundabout?
options: A driver in the inner lane might switch outward or a cyclist might be riding there
The outer lane is always closed
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 advises watching all circulating lanes and cyclists before entering.

questions.question: What sign sits on the central island facing approaching traffic on many roundabouts?
options: A blue sign with white keep-left arrows or white chevrons pointing left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 uses keep-left arrows and chevrons to guide traffic clockwise.
